issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may condition a stay of an eviction order on payment of reasonable compensation for continued occupation, even when that compensation exceeds the contractual rent.
material_facts: The tenant appealed an eviction order and sought to remain in possession while the appeal was pending.
The tribunal stayed eviction on condition that the tenant make monthly deposits in addition to the contractual rent, with the deposits held until the appeal was decided.
The premises were commercial property, the contractual rent had remained very low for decades, and evidence indicated that comparable nearby premises were let at substantially higher rent.
The tenant did not contend that the amount fixed by the tribunal was unreasonable or grossly excessive.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal had power to condition the stay on reasonable compensation for the landlord’s loss from delayed execution, and the High Court erred in setting aside the condition solely because it exceeded the contractual rent. The tribunal’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 38(3) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, the tribunal has the powers of a court under the Code of Civil Procedure, including the power under Order 41 Rule 5 to stay execution. A stay is discretionary and equitable, not an automatic right; Order 41 Rule 5(3) requires consideration of substantial loss, delay, and security. The court may impose reasonable terms to compensate the successful decree-holder for loss caused by the stay. South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. v. State of M.P. supports restorative compensation for benefits or losses resulting from interim orders; Marshall Sons & Co. (I) Ltd. v. Sahi Oretrans (P) Ltd. supports reasonable mesne profits, potentially equivalent to market rent, when execution of a possession decree is delayed. The court may also consider common knowledge and judicially noticeable facts, as recognized in Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation.

rule.if: eviction_appeal_stay_application and eviction_order_under_appeal and tenant_seeks_continued_occupation and landlord_succeeded_below

predicates.eviction_appeal_stay_application: A party pursued an appeal from an eviction order and asked the appellate court to stay its execution.
predicates.eviction_order_under_appeal: An eviction order had been made against the party seeking the stay.
predicates.tenant_seeks_continued_occupation: The tenant sought to remain in occupation while the appeal was pending.
predicates.landlord_succeeded_below: The landlord had obtained the eviction order from the lower forum.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks to remain in occupation during an appeal from an eviction order obtained by the landlord, the stay may be conditioned on reasonable compensation for occupation.

issues.legal_issue: Under rent-control legislation whose definition of tenant excludes a person against whom an eviction order has been made, the tenancy ends when the eviction order is made, rather than when appellate proceedings conclude.
material_facts: The premises were governed by the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.
The statutory definition of tenant included a person continuing in possession after termination of tenancy but excluded a person against whom an order or decree for eviction had been made.
An eviction order had been made against the tenant, who continued in possession while challenging it.
issues.conclusion: For premises governed by the Act, the tenancy ends upon the eviction order; if that order is maintained, the tenant’s continued occupation is unauthorized and liability for use and occupation is measured by what the landlord could have earned by letting the premises, not by the contractual rent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(l) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 includes certain persons continuing in possession after termination of tenancy but excludes a person against whom an eviction order or decree has been made. The court distinguished Chander Kali Bai v. Jagdish Singh Thakur, which turned on the wording of a different rent-control statute, and referred to Shyam Sharan v. Sheoji Bhai and Bhagwandas v. Mst. Kokabai in recognizing that a person continuing in occupation after the relevant termination may be liable for damages or mesne profits, with the rent-control ceiling not controlling their measure. The measure may reflect the rent the landlord could have earned if the premises had been vacated.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_appeal: A tenant pursued an appeal from an eviction order concerning premises governed by rent-control protections.
predicates.eviction_order_made: A lower forum made an order requiring the tenant’s eviction.
predicates.eviction_order_maintained: The eviction order remained in force after the challenge to it was decided.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction order is made and later maintained, the tenancy ends on the date of the initial eviction order.

issues.legal_issue: The doctrine of merger does not postpone the termination of a tenancy to the date on which a superior forum affirms an eviction order.
material_facts: An eviction order was made against a tenant of premises governed by the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.
The tenant challenged the order before a superior forum, and the order was subsequently maintained.
The tenant argued that merger in the superior forum’s order postponed the date on which the tenancy ended.
issues.conclusion: Affirmance by a superior forum does not, by operation of the doctrine of merger, postpone the termination of the tenancy from the date of the original eviction order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(l) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 excludes a person against whom an eviction order or decree has been made from the definition of tenant. Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala recognizes that the doctrine of merger is not universal or unlimited. Applying that qualification, the court held that merger in a later superior order does not change the fact that the original eviction order determined the date on which the tenancy ended; the effect of that order may be suspended while a stay operates.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_appeal: A tenant pursued an appeal from an eviction order concerning rent-controlled premises.
predicates.initial_eviction_order_made: A lower forum first made an order requiring the tenant’s eviction.
predicates.initial_eviction_order_later_maintained: A superior forum later left the initial eviction order in force.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction order is later maintained on appeal, merger does not move the tenancy-termination point from the initial eviction order to the superior forum’s order.
